H&P – Detailed Note

Consult Summary:
29-year-old woman with no significant past medical history other than remote kidney stones presents with a first-episode, sudden-onset left-sided headache with visual aura, nausea and vomiting, clinically consistent with an acute migraine; advised analgesia/anti-emetic regimen and same-day practice review for formal neurological examination.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden, severe headache beginning ~4 hours prior to consult.  
• Character: Unilateral (left-sided), intensity 6/10 compared with prior kidney-stone pain.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Blurred vision described as “zig-zag lines.”  
  – Dizziness.  
  – Nausea with two episodes of vomiting at onset; ongoing nausea.  
  – Worsens with movement; prefers to keep head still; cannot tolerate screens.  
• Tried self-care: Single dose paracetamol ~3 h ago with no relief.  
• Denies: Limb weakness, gait disturbance, other focal neurological deficits.  
• First episode of this type of headache; no prior migraines personally.

Past Medical History:
• Kidney stones (remote episode; dates/details not provided).  
• No known chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• None on a regular basis.  
• Paracetamol (self-administered today; dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Pregnancy unlikely (patient statement).  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use, occupation, and living circumstances not discussed.

Family History:
• Mother: Migraines; hypothyroidism.  
• No other relevant family conditions reported.

Physical Examination:
• No in-person examination performed (teleconsultation).  
• Vitals not obtained.

Investigations:
• None performed/reported during call.

Assessment & Plan:

Issue 1: Acute unilateral headache with aura – likely migraine
• Features (unilateral pain, visual disturbance, nausea/vomiting) typical for migraine.  
• Differential: less likely intracranial pathology given absence of focal deficits, but in-person review arranged out of caution.

Plan:  
  – Trial ibuprofen (dose/route not documented) plus over-the-counter anti-sickness medication.  
  – Encourage oral intake of sugary, carbonated drink (e.g., cola).  
  – If inadequate response, escalate to specific migraine therapies (triptans) per GP review.  
  – Same-day appointment arranged for full neurological examination; attend earlier or A&E if symptoms worsen (e.g., escalating pain, new neurological signs).  
  – If symptoms resolve before appointment, patient may cancel.

Issue 2: Nausea and vomiting
• Likely secondary to migraine.

Plan:  
  – OTC anti-emetic with analgesic as above.  
  – Maintain hydration.

Issue 3: Health anxiety
• Patient worried about brain tumour/stroke.

Plan:  
  – Provided reassurance regarding migraine diagnosis and planned examination.  
  – Advised to seek immediate care if new concerning symptoms appear.

General Plan Items:
• Provide written migraine information sheet and headache diary at in-person visit.  
• Discuss lifestyle triggers and long-term prophylaxis if recurrent.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: vitals, full neurological & fundoscopic examination, detailed social history, medication reconciliation beyond paracetamol, exact dosages for recommended drugs.  
• No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
• Transcript quality: clear; minor connectivity interruptions but clinically sufficient.
